subproblem.title: Monotonicity with bounded mean curvature (Simon 4.3.17): densities exist and are upper semicontinuous
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, n ≥ 1, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) represented by R = (M, θ, ξ) (IMRep U n), and suppose the varifold V = v(M, θ) has locally bounded generalized mean curvature in U (IMRep.HasLocallyBoundedMeanCurvature: there is H, a.e. strongly measurable for μ := μ_R, with ‖H‖ essentially bounded on every compact K ⊆ U, such that ∫_M θ div_M X dHⁿ = −∫ X·H dμ for every C¹ vector field X with compact support in U, div_M X(y) = trace(p_{T_yM}∘DX(y))). Then there is Θ : ℝ^P → ℝ such that HasMassDensity T x (Θ x) for every x ∈ U (Θ(x) ≥ 0 and M_{B_ρ(x)}(T)/(ω_nρⁿ) → Θ(x) as ρ ↓ 0, ω_n = unitBallVolume n) and Θ is upper semicontinuous on U.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → 0 < n → R.Represents T → R.HasLocallyBoundedMeanCurvature → ∃ Θ : Euclid P → ℝ, (∀ x ∈ U, HasMassDensity T x (Θ x)) ∧ UpperSemicontinuousOn Θ U
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: proof of Simon 7.3.1, first sentence (chapter-07.txt lines 326–328: "apply the monotonicity formula ... to deduce that Θⁿ(T, x) exists for every x ∈ U and is an upper semi-continuous function"), with the monotonicity formula of Ch. 4, 3.1–3.4 and 3.14–3.17 and the upper semicontinuity argument of Ch. 4, 3.11 (chapter-04.txt lines 215–345, 370–420); step 3 of the parent proof. Uses the sibling mass_eq_measure. (A formal version of steps 2–5 for SimonGMT's RectifiableVarifold is Chapter04/MeanCurvature.lean, exp_normalizedBallMass_monotoneOn and upperSemicontinuousOn_stationaryDensity; the printed sign in 4.3.16 is corrected there, and only the absolute bound on the error term is used below.) Write μ := μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M; for y ∈ M where T_yM exists, p_y denotes orthogonal projection onto T_yM and div_M X(y) = trace(p_y∘DX(y)).
0. The first variation is a genuine Lebesgue integral. For increasing (n−1)-indices J let e^J be the basic (n−1)-covector (for n = 1, e^∅ = 1), and for v ∈ ℝ^P let v^♭ ∧ e^J be the n-covector (u₁,…,uₙ) ↦ Σ_b (−1)^{b−1}⟨v, u_b⟩e^J(u₁,…,û_b,…,uₙ). If ζ(α) = ±α(τ₁,…,τₙ) for an orthonormal frame τ of an n-dimensional subspace Q, then Σ_J ζ(v^♭∧e^J)ζ(w^♭∧e^J) = Σ_{b,b'}(−1)^{b+b'}⟨v,τ_b⟩⟨w,τ_{b'}⟩Σ_J e^J(τ_{≠b})e^J(τ_{≠b'}) = Σ_b⟨v,τ_b⟩⟨w,τ_b⟩ = ⟨p_Q v, w⟩, because by the Cauchy–Binet formula Σ_J e^J(τ_{≠b})e^J(τ_{≠b'}) is the determinant of the Gram matrix (⟨τ_i, τ_{i'}⟩)_{i≠b, i'≠b'}, which is 1 if b = b' and 0 otherwise (if b ≠ b', the row of τ_{b'} vanishes). Hence for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M the orthogonal projection p_y onto T_yM = approxTangentPlane n M y (which exists and is unique a.e. by the field `orients` and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique) equals Π(ξ(y)), where Π(ζ) is the linear map with ⟨Π(ζ)v, w⟩ = Σ_J ζ(v^♭∧e^J)ζ(w^♭∧e^J), a continuous (quadratic) function of ζ. So y ↦ p_y is a.e. strongly measurable on M, and for a C¹ field X with compact support in U the function y ↦ θ(y)·trace(p_y∘DX(y)) (= θ·tangentialDivergence n M X) is a.e. strongly measurable and bounded by n·sup‖DX‖·θ·1_{spt X}, which is integrable on M because spt X is a compact subset of U. Thus R.firstVariation X = ∫ div_M X dμ is the integral of an integrable function, and the first-variation hypothesis is a genuine identity of integrals.
1. Localization of the bound. Fix ξ₀ ∈ U and R₀ > 0 with closedBall(ξ₀, 2R₀) ⊆ U, and let Λ ≥ 0 be such that ‖H‖ ≤ Λ μ-a.e. on K₀ := closedBall(ξ₀, 2R₀) (hypothesis). For every ξ ∈ ball(ξ₀, R₀), closedBall(ξ, R₀) ⊆ K₀; μ(K₀) < ∞ by local integrability.
2. Monotonicity (Ch. 4, 3.2–3.4, 3.16–3.17). Let ξ ∈ ball(ξ₀, R₀), r(y) := |y − ξ|, ε ∈ (0,1), and let φ_ε : ℝ → [0,1] be C¹ and nonincreasing with φ_ε = 1 on (−∞, 1], φ_ε = 0 on [1 + ε, ∞), chosen so that φ_ε decreases pointwise to 1_{(−∞,1]} as ε ↓ 0 (e.g. φ_ε(t) = φ₁(1 + (t − 1)/ε) for t ≥ 1). For 0 < ρ < R₀/(1 + ε) the field X(y) := φ_ε(r/ρ)(y − ξ) is C¹ (φ_ε is constant near 0) with support in closedBall(ξ, (1+ε)ρ) ⊆ U. At y ∈ M where T_yM exists and y ≠ ξ, DX = φ_ε(r/ρ)·Id + (φ_ε'(r/ρ)/(ρr))(y − ξ)⊗(y − ξ), so div_M X = nφ_ε(r/ρ) + (r/ρ)φ_ε'(r/ρ)(1 − |D^⊥r|²), where D^⊥r := (Id − p_y)((y − ξ)/r) (Ch. 4, 3.2); at y = ξ, DX = Id and the same formula holds with D^⊥r(ξ) := 0 (φ_ε'(0) = 0); in any case {ξ} is μ-null since Hⁿ({ξ}) = 0 for n ≥ 1. Put I(ρ) := ∫φ_ε(r/ρ) dμ, J(ρ) := ∫φ_ε(r/ρ)|D^⊥r|² dμ and E(ρ) := ∫φ_ε(r/ρ)(y − ξ)·H dμ. Since ∂_ρ[φ_ε(r/ρ)] = −(r/ρ²)φ_ε'(r/ρ) is continuous in ρ and bounded by c/ρ on {r ≤ (1+ε)ρ}, dominated convergence shows I, J ∈ C¹ on (0, R₀/(1+ε)) with derivatives obtained by differentiating under the integral; J is nondecreasing (φ_ε(r/ρ) is nondecreasing in ρ). Because (r/ρ)φ_ε'(r/ρ) = −ρ∂_ρ[φ_ε(r/ρ)], the identity ∫ div_M X dμ = −∫ X·H dμ (step 0 and the hypothesis) reads nI(ρ) − ρI'(ρ) + ρJ'(ρ) = −E(ρ), i.e. d/dρ(ρ^{−n}I(ρ)) = ρ^{−n}J'(ρ) + ρ^{−n−1}E(ρ). On spt φ_ε(r/ρ) ⊆ closedBall(ξ, (1+ε)ρ) ⊆ K₀ we have |(y − ξ)·H| ≤ (1+ε)ρΛ μ-a.e., so |E(ρ)| ≤ Λ_ερ·I(ρ) with Λ_ε := (1+ε)Λ. Hence d/dρ(e^{Λ_ερ}ρ^{−n}I(ρ)) = e^{Λ_ερ}(d/dρ(ρ^{−n}I) + Λ_ερ^{−n}I) ≥ e^{Λ_ερ}ρ^{−n}J'(ρ) ≥ 0, and ρ ↦ e^{Λ_ερ}ρ^{−n}I(ρ) is nondecreasing on (0, R₀/(1+ε)). Given 0 < σ < ρ < R₀, choose ε₀ with ρ < R₀/(1+ε₀); for ε ≤ ε₀ along a sequence ε ↓ 0, φ_ε(r/t) ↓ 1_{closedBall(ξ,t)} pointwise, dominated by 1_{K₀}, so I(t) → μ(closedBall(ξ, t)) for t = σ, ρ and Λ_ε → Λ. Therefore g_ξ(t) := e^{Λt}t^{−n}μ(closedBall(ξ, t)) is nondecreasing on (0, R₀) (Ch. 4, 3.17 with F(t) ∈ [e^{−Λt}, e^{Λt}]).
3. Existence of the density. For ξ ∈ ball(ξ₀, R₀), g_ξ ≥ 0 is nondecreasing on (0, R₀), so L(ξ) := lim_{t↓0} g_ξ(t) = inf g_ξ exists in [0, ∞); as e^{Λt} → 1, t^{−n}μ(closedBall(ξ, t)) → L(ξ). For open balls, μ(closedBall(ξ, t/(1+δ))) ≤ μ(ball(ξ, t)) ≤ μ(closedBall(ξ, t)) for δ > 0, so lim inf and lim sup of t^{−n}μ(ball(ξ, t)) lie between (1+δ)^{−n}L(ξ) and L(ξ); letting δ ↓ 0, t^{−n}μ(ball(ξ, t)) → L(ξ). The limit does not depend on the choice of ξ₀, R₀. Every ξ ∈ U lies in such a ball (take ξ₀ = ξ), so define Θ(ξ) := L(ξ)/ω_n for ξ ∈ U (ω_n = unitBallVolume n ∈ (0, ∞)) and Θ(ξ) := 0 for ξ ∉ U.
4. HasMassDensity. Let x ∈ U and s > 0 with ball(x, s) ⊆ U. For 0 < ρ < s, mass_eq_measure gives M_{B_ρ(x)}(T) = μ(ball(x, ρ)), so M_{B_ρ(x)}(T)/(ω_n·ρⁿ) = (ρ^{−n}μ(ball(x, ρ)))/ω_n → L(x)/ω_n = Θ(x) as ρ ↓ 0 (all quantities finite; the convergence holds in [0, ∞] with ofReal Θ(x)). Also Θ(x) ≥ 0. So HasMassDensity T x (Θ x).
5. Upper semicontinuity (Ch. 4, 3.11). Fix ξ ∈ U, take ξ₀ := ξ and R₀, Λ as in step 1, and let ξ_j → ξ with ξ_j ∈ U. Let t > 0 and δ > 0 with t + δ < R₀/2. For all large j, |ξ_j − ξ| < δ and ξ_j ∈ ball(ξ, R₀), so by step 2 for the centre ξ_j (same K₀ and Λ), ω_nΘ(ξ_j) = L(ξ_j) ≤ g_{ξ_j}(t) = e^{Λt}t^{−n}μ(closedBall(ξ_j, t)) ≤ e^{Λt}t^{−n}μ(closedBall(ξ, t + δ)). Hence lim sup_j Θ(ξ_j) ≤ e^{Λt}t^{−n}μ(closedBall(ξ, t + δ))/ω_n. Letting δ ↓ 0 (μ(closedBall(ξ, t + δ)) ↓ μ(closedBall(ξ, t)), finite measure, continuity from above) and then t ↓ 0 (step 3) gives lim sup_j Θ(ξ_j) ≤ Θ(ξ). In the metric space ℝ^P this sequential statement at every ξ ∈ U is UpperSemicontinuousOn Θ U.
proof_key_steps: Test the first-variation identity with the radial fields φ(r/ρ)(y − ξ): d/dρ(ρ^{−n}I) = ρ^{−n}J' + ρ^{−n−1}E with |E| ≤ (1+ε)Λρ I.
Hence e^{Λρ}ρ^{−n}μ(B̄_ρ(ξ)) is nondecreasing near every point, so the density limit exists and is finite; open and closed balls give the same limit.
mass_eq_measure converts μ(B_ρ(x)) into M_{B_ρ(x)}(T), giving HasMassDensity.
Monotonicity at nearby centres yields upper semicontinuity (Simon 4.3.11 argument).

audit.reason: The proof justifies projection measurability and integrability before applying the first-variation identity. Radial testing gives finite density limits, and a common local curvature bound gives upper semicontinuity at nearby centres. The mass identity supplies exactly HasMassDensity.
